title: Any easy solutions for adding online multiplayer to your game?
author: IllustriousTip6904
selftext: I've been dreaming up games in Claude, some of which are multiplayer. Claude frequently flags online multiplayer as being some huge endeavor with lots of complicating factors. I'm wondering if there's any solutions out there that make this less intimidating, maybe even easy.

comments.author: flukeytukey
comments.body:
Nothing easy no. Depends on your experience and platform. Eg I used Opus whatever to build your basic friendslop game with prox chat and lobbies and smooth multiplayer (distributed authority) in Unity in about 2 weeks. 

I could only do that because I've already spent years making every mistake building multiplayer improperly in Unity, so I had experience and the power of Claude to build it properly from scratch. 

You could still probably get Claude to do this but you should invest your own actual time researching. Always easier to start with multiplayer rather than add it.

replies.author: PersonOfInterest007
replies.body: I’d suggest starting with old-fashioned Google, or of course you can ask your favorite LLM. There are various choices depending on which game engine you’re using.

replies.author: PersonOfInterest007
replies.body:
Here’s just one example for Godot: https://www.gd-sync.com/

For Unreal, it looks like Epic has a “Lyra Starter Game” that’s often used as a template: https://dev.epicgames.com/community/learning/paths/Z4/lyra-starter-game

You can also find paid Unreal templates on FAB, eg https://www.fab.com/search/channels/unreal-engine?q=Multiplayer

But I’d really start with Google or with an LLM prompt like “What premade assets or systems exist to help build a multiplayer game in Unreal Engine?”

There are solutions for specific types of multiplayer (eg an FPS), or others that are designed for generic lobby support or certain patterns of game synchronization (eg friendslop local multiplayer vs online multiplayer lobbies).  So you’ll probably get a better answer if you’ve described your type of game and then ask for what solutions are already available.

replies.author: PersonOfInterest007
replies.body:
Here’s ChatGPT’s response for just my first stab at a question for Unreal: https://chatgpt.com/share/6a7cda02-40c8-83ea-bca4-b4a609cbc38a

Do keep in mind that multiplayer really is nontrivial. But starting with  something that’s already built and tested is going to be far more robust than having an LLM create one from scratch. The number of pitfalls for a multiplayer game is very large.

Here’s a chat I created with ChatGPT, both to ask it was was available to use with Godot, but also specifically how it would recommend creating prompts for Claude that would get Claude to help create an architecture for a game that would incorporate potential prebuilt assets: https://chatgpt.com/share/6a7cdd20-616c-83ea-a05c-3e7b8fbf8c70

comments.author: RoyalSpecialist1777
comments.body:
Depending on how many player you want, before implementing whatever architecture you come up with Claude think about network communication costs when synchronizing the world between players.  Opus was not thinking and it's proposed plan would have tanked after more than a few players.  
  
I have built a massive multiplayer game with thousands of shared game objects that are synchronized across clients - clients use determinism to get identical behavior with the server relaying events to each other like when a player moves to another cell or changes the world somehow.  I think it's called a frontier gated deterministic tick system or something. This is paired with Nakama which makes some things easier. 

With Opus and human in the loop development it actually took a couple weeks as it is not simple and now works very well.  We needed to document every aspect in a skill Claude could read because any changes to the game potentially needed to integrate into this system.  That said the later Opus versions had way less issues with it.

So this would not be a 'in one session' task but also something doable with guidance in probably a week with the later Claude models and a few sessions.  Or if you are sloppy it might take weeks.
